correctness.rationale: Every cube antipodal geodesic corresponds bijectively to one permutation. The deleted weight-k vertex excludes exactly those having first-k label set A. Swapping consecutive flips is exactly one legal rerouting move. Strictly increasing B-before-A cross inversions connects each surviving ordering to a canonical B-block/A-block ordering; internal swaps connect all canonical block orderings. The deleted permutahedron facet has F=k!(n-k)! vertices, each of internal degree n-2 and exactly one distinct external neighbor, yielding the stated degree and edge census. At k=1 or n-1 ordinary insertion sorting always keeps the unique banned first/last label away from that endpoint and uses exactly the Kendall number of moves. At interior k, the four-letter witness has Kendall distance four, but a Kendall geodesic would have to cross the forbidden facet because its only two feasible cross-inversion witnesses cannot coexist while the common pair orders are preserved; a six-step valid sequence achieves distance six and parity excludes five. Conditions n>=2, 1<=k<=n-1 are covered, including boundary n=2. Actual graph checker reconciles cube paths and adjacent swaps, and exhaustive checks through n=6 corroborate all-pairs claims; it does not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The original hypercube rerouting theorem fixes unrestricted Kendall distance, while the new claim concerns deleting one specified intermediate cube state, which removes a whole facet of the permutation reconfiguration graph. The established face-convexity theorem concerns geodesics with both endpoints inside a face, not the complement. Classic fault-tolerant cube routing addresses underlying routes after faults, not paths between the admissible shortest routes. Primary full-text relevant sections, exact title/alias searches, and published related findings did not provide the weight-layer connectivity/geodesic-loss dichotomy or its explicit six-versus-four witness. The negative search is not a proof of global novelty; unindexed literature remains a risk.

value.rationale: The object is the canonical network-routing shortest-path reconfiguration graph of a Boolean interconnection network under one failed intermediate node. The result supplies a sharp, complete failure-layer classification: connectivity always survives, all-pairs optimality survives exactly for failures one step from an endpoint, and a forced two-step rerouting detour appears at every deeper failure layer, with n=4 as sharp onset. It also quantifies every surviving route and all reconfiguration edges and vertex degree losses. The outcome is a nontrivial structural boundary between reachability and metric resilience rather than a new name for a known count; it can guide fault-aware route updates. It does not claim a general worst-case penalty bound.
